from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite Review: Determinants as Area", [
            "Determinants measure the area of parallelograms.",
            "Columns of A define a base parallelogram.",
            "Determinants represent this total signed area."
        ])
        
        # Axes for the parallelogram
        axes = Axes(x_range=[-1, 4, 1], y_range=[-1, 4, 1], axis_config={"include_tip": True}).scale(0.5)
        self.place_in_area(axes, 'B2', 'E5', scale_factor=0.7)
        
        u = np.array([2, 0, 0])
        v = np.array([0, 2, 0])
        
        vec_u = Vector(u, color="#FF5733")
        vec_v = Vector(v, color="#33FF57")
        
        # Parallelogram using Polygon
        points = [ORIGIN, u, u + v, v]
        para = Polygon(*points, color=BLUE, fill_opacity=0.3)
        para.shift(axes.c2p(0, 0) - ORIGIN)
        
        # Ensure vectors are aligned with axes
        vec_u.put_start_and_end_on(axes.c2p(0, 0), axes.c2p(*u[:2]))
        vec_v.put_start_and_end_on(axes.c2p(0, 0), axes.c2p(*v[:2]))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFF99")
        self.play(Create(axes), Create(vec_u), Create(vec_v), FadeIn(para))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FFFF99")
        # No extra animation here, the objects are already created

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFFF99")
        formula = MathTex(r"|\det(A)| = \text{area} = 4").scale(0.8).set_color(WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(formula, 'F3')
        self.play(Write(formula))
        self.play(Indicate(para, color="#FFFF00"), Indicate(formula, color="#FFFF00"))
        self.wait(2)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Visualizing the Linear System", [
            "Represent Ax = b as vector combinations.",
            "Basis vectors a1 and a2 reach b.",
            "Find x and y scaling factors."
        ])
        
        # Setup Axes
        axes = Axes(x_range=[-1, 6, 1], y_range=[-1, 6, 1], x_length=4, y_length=4).scale(0.6)
        
        a1 = Vector([1, 0], color="#FF5733")
        a2 = Vector([0, 1], color="#33FF57")
        b = Vector([5, 5], color=WHITE)
        
        # Grouping for layout
        system_group = VGroup(axes, a1, a2, b)
        self.place_in_area(system_group, 'B2', 'E5', scale_factor=0.8)
        
        self.add(axes)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.play(GrowArrow(a1), GrowArrow(a2))
        self.play(GrowArrow(b))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        # Visual highlighting
        a1_label = MathTex("a_1", color="#FF5733").next_to(a1.get_end(), RIGHT)
        a2_label = MathTex("a_2", color="#33FF57").next_to(a2.get_end(), UP)
        self.play(Write(a1_label), Write(a2_label))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Visualizing x*a1 + y*a2 = b
        x_val = ValueTracker(0)
        y_val = ValueTracker(0)
        
        v1 = always_redraw(lambda: Vector(x_val.get_value() * np.array([1, 0]), color="#FF5733"))
        v2 = always_redraw(lambda: Vector(y_val.get_value() * np.array([0, 1]), color="#33FF57"))
        
        self.add(v1, v2)
        self.play(x_val.animate.set_value(5), y_val.animate.set_value(5), run_time=2)
        
        self.wait(1)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Replace column a1 with target vector b.",
            "New parallelogram formed by b and a2.",
            "Ratio of areas gives scaling factor x.",
            "Cramer's Rule equals area ratio calculation.",
            "This reveals x coordinate geometrically."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Geometric Derivation of Cramer's Rule", lecture_lines)
        
        # Colors
        colors = ["#FF7F50", "#87CEFA", "#90EE90", "#FFD700", "#FF69B4"]
        
        # --- Define Mobjects ---
        # Area (b, a2)
        plane = NumberPlane(x_range=[-1, 3], y_range=[-1, 3]).scale(0.5)
        self.place_in_area(plane, 'B2', 'E5', scale_factor=1.0)
        
        b = Vector([2, 1], color=RED)
        a2 = Vector([0, 2], color=BLUE)
        a1 = Vector([1, 0], color=GREEN)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(colors[0])
        self.play(Create(plane), Create(b), Create(a2))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(colors[1])
        # Parallelogram formed by b, a2
        poly = Polygon(ORIGIN, b.get_end(), b.get_end() + a2.get_end(), a2.get_end(), fill_opacity=0.3, color=BLUE)
        self.add(poly)
        self.wait(1)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(colors[2])
        label = MathTex(r"Area = |det(b, a2)|").scale(0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(label, 'B6')
        self.play(Write(label))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color(colors[3])
        ratio = MathTex(r"x_1 = \frac{det(b, a2)}{det(a1, a2)}").scale(0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(ratio, 'E6')
        self.play(FadeIn(ratio))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[4].set_color(colors[4])
        self.play(Indicate(ratio, color=YELLOW))
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Summary and Intuition", [
            "Cramer's rule is geometric area scaling.",
            "Each factor represents an area ratio.",
            "Intuitive way to solve linear systems."
        ])
        
        # Animations
        # Cramer's Rule Formula: x_i = det(A_i) / det(A)
        cramer_formula = MathTex(r"x_i = \frac{\det(A_i)}{\det(A)}", font_size=40, color=WHITE)
        self.place_in_area(cramer_formula, 'B2', 'C5')
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(cramer_formula))
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#00FFFF"))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Represent area ratio
        ratio_viz = VGroup(
            Square(color=BLUE, fill_opacity=0.5).scale(0.5),
            Text("/", font_size=24),
            Square(color=RED, fill_opacity=0.5).scale(0.8)
        ).arrange(RIGHT)
        self.place_in_area(ratio_viz, 'D2', 'E5')
        self.play(Create(ratio_viz))
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FF00FF"))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Flash the rule
        self.play(Indicate(cramer_formula, color="#FFFF00"))
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FFFF00"))
        self.wait(2)

sections.title: Prerequisite Review: Determinants as Area
sections.content: Briefly define the determinant of a 2x2 matrix as the 'signed area' of a parallelogram formed by two vectors (column vectors of the matrix). Explain that the sign indicates orientation.
sections.example: Vectors u=(2,0) and v=(0,2) form a square with area 4. The determinant |A| = 4.

sections.title: Visualizing the Linear System
sections.content: Represent the system Ax = b as a vector combination: x(a1) + y(a2) = b, where a1, a2 are column vectors. Show how the solution (x, y) represents scaling factors for these basis vectors.
sections.example: A robot arm needs to reach point b(5,5). It uses two motors represented by vectors a1(1,0) and a2(0,1). The system solves how much to scale each motor.

sections.title: Geometric Derivation of Cramer's Rule
sections.content: Explain that replacing a column of A with b creates a new parallelogram. Show that the ratio of the area of this new parallelogram to the original |A| equals the scaling factor of the missing vector.
sections.example: For x*a1 + y*a2 = b, the area of the parallelogram formed by (b, a2) is exactly x times the area of (a1, a2). Thus, x = det(b, a2) / det(a1, a2).

sections.title: Summary and Intuition
sections.content: Consolidate the concept: Cramer's rule is simply an area-ratio calculation. It tells us how much 'space' the vector b occupies relative to the transformation defined by matrix A.
sections.example: A chef balancing two ingredient vectors (a1, a2) to hit a target nutrient profile (b). Cramer's rule finds the exact 'weight' of each ingredient via geometric scaling.
